answer: The comparison is not precisely recoverable from memory, so this is a hedged summary. In the LINE paper (Tang et al., 2015), LINE(1st) and LINE(2nd) both improve as the number of edge samples grows and then plateau. LINE(1st), which models only first-order proximity, tends to reach its plateau sooner, while LINE(2nd) usually needs more samples but reaches a higher final quality. DeepWalk is trained on random-walk corpora with skip-gram and SGD; the paper reports it as competitive in accuracy but slower in wall-clock training time than LINE, so LINE's advantage is mainly efficiency rather than a large accuracy gap. Exact curves depend on the dataset and should be checked against the paper's figures.
